source_excerpts.text:
## Model

A single source reservoir has constant heat capacity C, temperature rise T0 above a fixed bath, and initial energy E=C*T0. It cools through an autonomous memoryless conductance G(T), with

    0<g_min<=G(T)<=g_max,    K=g_max/g_min>1.

There is no subsequent input or independent clock. The normalized bath-flux distribution is the full released energy, including off-state leakage. Let its mean be m and variance V. Overall timescale rescaling does not change V/m^2.

Writing u=T/T0 and z=-log u, conservation says normalized released energy is -du. Therefore Z=-log U is an Exp(1) variable and the release-time random variable is

    t(Z),  t(z)=integral_0^z a(s)ds,
    a(s)=C/G(T0*exp(-s)).

Rescale time so a is in [1/K,1]. This is an exact representation of the model, not a stochastic material mechanism.

## The exact global optimum

Among every measurable conductance curve in the allowed range, the smallest squared coefficient of variation v=V/m^2 is the unique solution v in (0,1) of

    2[atanh(v)-v] = -log(1-1/K)-1/K.                     (1)

An attaining memoryless curve is a single threshold: G=g_min initially, then G=g_max after the reservoir cools to eta*T0, where

    eta=(1-v)/[(1+v)(1-1/K)].                           (2)

For continuous curves with no bound on slope this is an infimum, approached by steep smooth transitions. A real actuator with bounded transition width/dynamics may do worse. The theorem optimizes the mathematical conductance curve; it does not supply a physical curve that was not measured.

## Derivation for a threshold

Let d=-log eta, a=1 before d, a=1/K afterward, and r=1-1/K. Its survival function has off-state decay until d and on-state decay afterward. Direct integration gives

    m=1-eta+eta/K,
    E[t^2]=2[1-eta(1+d)+eta(d/K+1/K^2)].                (3)

Set y=r*eta. Then m=1-y and E[t^2]=2[1-y(1+1/K+log(r/y))]. Differentiating E[t^2]/m^2 with respect to y shows the unique stationary point satisfies

    1+1/K+log(r/y)=(3-y)/(1+y).                         (4)

The derivative of the left side minus right side is

    -(1-y)^2/[y(1+y)^2]<0.

It tends to positive infinity at y=0 and is negative at y=r, so the root is unique in the physical interval. At this point

    v=(1-y)/(1+y).

Substituting in (4) gives (1),(2). All endpoint cases have CV squared 1, so this is the unique threshold optimum.

## Global certificate

## Q17: existing optimization, a geometric qualification and a new ideal frontier

The full tree proof remains sound at its stated positive-real scope. Stage2 additionally gives a concrete strongest competing explanation: under `x_i=log(S_i)`, thermal normalized edge-delay weights solve exactly generalized least squares for estimating a constant with OU covariance `exp(-|x_i-x_j|)`. I checked that mapping. The [authors' primary institutional abstract for Kiselak–Stehlik (2008)](https://research.jku.at/en/publications/equidistant-and-d-optimal-designs-for-parameters-of-ornstein-uhle-2/) explicitly attributes n-point equidistant D-optimality for the trend parameter to that work. The complete paper was inaccessible in my lookup. The shared optimization/equidistance principle is nevertheless an established antecedent, not a new foundational principle; the thermal/tree interpretation's application-level priority remains unknown.

[AUDIT.md §3](../../review_material/Q17/stage2/AUDIT.md) also correctly qualifies the earlier continuum realization. Substituting its fixed area and diffusion length gives `chi=a_max/ell=sqrt(C_total/(pi*c_v*ell^3))`. At fixed material, capacity and delay, geometric similarity cannot independently make this small. I accept that correction to the physical reach of the preserved stage1 statement. The ideal one-dimensional transfer equation and finite-tree theorem survive, conditional on the actual geometry regime.

The substantive new claim in [SWITCH_PROOF.md](../../review_material/Q17/stage2/SWITCH_PROOF.md) optimizes every measurable memoryless conductance curve between fixed positive limits. I reconstructed the energy-coordinate map `t(Z)`, `Z~Exp(1)`, the unique threshold stationary equation, and the global linear-functional/Cauchy–Schwarz certificate. Its functional coefficient changes sign once at the candidate threshold, so the box-constrained threshold minimizes that functional over all curves. This establishes the full-function optimum, not merely an optimized step fixture. The parameter `v` is CV squared. The `K^(-1/3)` CV asymptotic, timescale qualification and charging barrier follow at the declared ideal scope.
